candidates.title: Seat a machined part with a self-locking lifting pin, then unlock and recover the pin
candidates.objective: Insert and mechanically lock a self-locking ball lifting pin in a machined workpiece, lift the workpiece through the movable shackle, seat it on a three-pad fixture, transfer its weight to the fixture, and withdraw the unloaded pin without displacing or dropping the part.
skills: coordinated button hold and axial withdrawal
candidates.success_conditions: Score begins at 0. Award 0.20 after the released button has returned to its initial position and the inserted pin resists a 10 mm guarded upward pull for 3.0 s; 0.45 after the locked pin alone supports a lift of at least 30 mm for 2.0 s; and 0.70 after the workpiece contacts all three fixture pads with every measured support gap at or below 2 mm. Award 1.00 only after the pin is completely outside the bore, the workpiece remains on all three pads, both grippers are at least 60 mm clear, and fresh 10 Hz observations confirm a 3.0 s dwell. Dropping either object, releasing the load outside the fixture boundary, losing a locking ball, or withdrawing the pin before fixture support permanently prevents full credit and caps the score at the highest safely completed stage. Loss of retention revokes the 0.20 and 0.45 stages. Any grasp, hand assignment, or action order is valid when the same physical prerequisites and outcomes hold. Physics validation separately records rigid-body, native-joint, and contact traces at 240 Hz; those diagnostics are not grading rules.
candidates.industrial_value: Halder describes EH 22350 as a heavy-duty temporary lifting element that needs only an H11 receiving bore and documents insertion, locking, removal, a movable shackle, and rated load directions. The task represents temporary lifting-hardware installation, workpiece transfer, fixture seating, unloading, and hardware recovery in manufacturing material handling rather than generic pick-and-place.
candidates.dexterity: High: the robot must align a nominal 10 mm pin with sub-millimetre diametral clearance, actuate a spring-return button, verify a real mechanical lock, grasp a freely moving shackle, control a suspended rigid load onto three supports, and hold the button while extracting the unloaded pin.

evidence.locator: EH 22350 data sheet, Product Description, page 1
EH 22350 data sheet, Drawing/order table, aligned row for article 22350.0621, page 2

candidates.asset_plan: Build an independently authored, full-scale rigid representative of EH 22350.0621 using the manufacturer diagrams: nominal d1 10.0 mm, l1 15 mm, mass 277 g, movable shackle, spring-return button, and collision-enabled radial locking balls. For buildable collision geometry, use a 9.94 mm shaft diameter, representing the published d1 tolerance band of 9.92–9.96 mm, and a 10.06 mm cylindrical workpiece bore, an explicitly chosen value within a nominal 10 mm H11-representative band; this gives 0.12 mm simulated diametral clearance. The representative 140×90×20 mm, 0.6 kg steel workpiece has a 2.0 mm lower retaining shoulder around the through-bore and sits on three 20×20 mm fixture pads. Model the button as a native prismatic joint with 3.0 mm test travel and a return spring; its internal cam drives three native radial ball sliders. Use 3.0 mm balls, 0.9 mm radial projection when locked, at least 0.15 mm retraction inside the 9.94 mm shaft envelope when fully pressed, and 0.10 mm collider clearance at each ball guide. Button travel, spring constant, ball size, cam profile, retaining-shoulder thickness, fixture dimensions, and selected H11 bore value are disclosed representative modeling assumptions, not manufacturer specifications. The acquired EH 22350 sheet establishes insertion/removal operation and the external retention concept but does not establish an under-load button prohibition; therefore the benchmark does not claim product-specific safety logic. It instead physically tests that support is present before extraction. Validate the mechanism first with no-op retention, unlocked pull-out, locked axial-load hold, pressed-button release, and unloaded extraction controls; then validate YAM access, one lift, fixture seating, and the complete guarded 14D demo. Preserve all essential colliders and use no object-state writes, fake grasp welds, or pose overrides.
candidates.risk: The closest known task places a hoisted motor on studs, whereas this objective additionally requires installing, mechanically locking, unloading, unlocking, and recovering temporary lifting hardware. Novelty still requires current corpus review. The internal cam and calibration are representative assumptions requiring native controls, and YAM access to the full-scale button and shackle remains a build-stage risk. No GN 1130 statement is used as EH 22350 evidence, and no EH 22350-specific under-load prohibition is asserted.

candidates.title: Install two self-locking lifting pins for balanced two-point placement
candidates.objective: Install and lock two self-locking lifting pins in opposite workpiece bores, lift the workpiece through both movable shackles while controlling its attitude, seat it on a fixture, and recover both unloaded pins.
candidates.success_conditions: Award 0.20 when both released-button pins independently withstand a 10 mm guarded pull for 3.0 s, 0.45 when both pins support a 30 mm lift with workpiece roll and pitch each within 5 degrees for 2.0 s, and 0.70 when all three fixture gaps are at most 2 mm. Full score requires complete withdrawal and release of both pins, both grippers 60 mm clear, and a fresh 3.0 s stable dwell. A dropped load, loss of either lock, permanent ball escape, or either extraction before fixture support prevents full credit. Hand assignment and extraction order are unrestricted.
candidates.industrial_value: The documented lifting element is designed to lift workpieces through a movable shackle and a simple receiving bore. Two independent temporary attachments make lock verification and load sharing consequential during placement of a rigid part.
candidates.dexterity: Very high: two close-clearance locks must be installed and verified before the arms coordinate a freely suspended two-point load, constrain roll and pitch during seating, and subsequently recover both pins.

evidence.locator: EH 22350 data sheet, Product Description, page 1

candidates.asset_plan: Use two independently articulated full-scale representative pins with the explicit 9.94 mm shaft and 10.06 mm bore collision dimensions defined for the selected candidate. The rigid plate, two bore locations, attachment geometry, and any intermediate support are representative fixture assumptions. Each shackle and gripper contact must transmit native forces; no virtual sling, fixed load distribution, weld, or task-object state write is permitted. Mechanism tests must precede any balancing demo.
candidates.risk: The source establishes each pin but does not specify this particular two-point rigging arrangement. With only two YAM grippers, installing two pins and then acquiring both shackles may require unsupported staging or an additional real tool, and the objective may collapse into an existing suspended-load placement ability.
missing_evidence: A source-grounded, physically reproducible two-point attachment arrangement for this workpiece
A feasible YAM regrasp or staging procedure that preserves both mechanical locks without artificial support
Current novelty evidence distinguishing balanced placement from existing suspended-load alignment tasks

candidates.title: Withdraw and cradle an unloaded self-locking lifting pin without disturbing the seated workpiece
candidates.objective: Stabilize a fixture-seated machined workpiece, fully depress and hold the lifting-pin button, extract the pin along the receiving-bore axis without scraping or shifting the workpiece, and place the recovered pin in a storage cradle.
skills: simultaneous button hold and axial pull
candidates.success_conditions: Award 0.25 while the button remains fully depressed for 1.0 s, 0.50 after the locking balls retract and the pin is withdrawn at least 10 mm, and 0.75 after complete extraction with workpiece translation at most 2 mm and rotation at most 2 degrees. Full score requires the pin released in its cradle, the workpiece still within those displacement limits, both grippers at least 60 mm clear, and a fresh 3.0 s dwell. Pulling while locked, dropping or ejecting the pin, exceeding 5 mm workpiece translation, or losing a ball prevents full credit. Equivalent stabilizing grasps and either hand assignment are valid.
candidates.industrial_value: The manufacturer explicitly specifies holding the button during removal of this temporary lifting element. Controlled axial recovery protects the receiving interface and leaves the seated workpiece undisturbed for subsequent manufacturing operations.
candidates.dexterity: Moderate to high: one arm must stabilize the workpiece while the other maintains a small spring-loaded control and pulls a shackle-equipped pin along a close-clearance axis before reorienting it into a cradle.
candidates.asset_plan: Use the same explicit 9.94 mm shaft and 10.06 mm bore collision diameters as the selected candidate, with the workpiece already supported on a rigid fixture. The cradle is a passive collision-enabled support and provides no artificial capture. Test locked-pull retention, full-button ball retraction, axial extraction, button-release relocking, and YAM reach before attempting the full sequence. Button travel, internal cam, ball geometry, and friction remain disclosed representative assumptions.
candidates.risk: Although source-grounded and easier to stage, removal alone may be judged generic locking-pin extraction rather than a sufficiently novel industrial ability. Native YAM simultaneous button actuation and axial pulling remain unverified.
missing_evidence: Current corpus evidence that button-held ball retraction and bore-preserving extraction are not a variant of generic pin removal
Native YAM reach and contact evidence for maintaining full button travel throughout axial extraction
A source or validated fixture rationale for the chosen disturbance and bore-protection limits

selection_reason: This is the only ready candidate that exercises the product sheet’s documented attachment, mechanical retention, lifting, fixture load transfer, removal, and hardware recovery in one coherent manufacturing cycle. It now avoids cross-manufacturer safety claims and specifies buildable shaft, bore, ball, shoulder, and guide collision geometry while clearly labeling every unpublished internal dimension as a testable representative assumption.
